'''Ronnie Brewer''' (born March 20, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and currently an assistant coach. Brewer played [[college basketball|collegiately]] at the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|University of Arkansas]], where his father [[Ron Brewer]] was a star in the late 1970s. Brewer is known for having an unorthodox shooting technique, the result of a childhood [[water slide]] injury.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/draft-central/notes061706-workouts.html Pre-Draft Workouts Resume in Waltham with Brewer]</ref>

The [[Utah Jazz]] selected him with the 14th pick of the [[2006 NBA draft]].

==College career==
Brewer played at Arkansas from 2003 to 2006 where he averaged 18.4 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 2.6 steals, and 0.5 blocks. He also was 51–151 from three-point range and shot 75% from the free-throw line.

==Professional career==

===Utah Jazz (2006–2010)===
Brewer was selected with the 14th pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]]. Brewer saw very limited playing time in his 2006–07 rookie season with Utah, appearing in only 56 games.  However, after a strong performance in the 2007–08 preseason,<ref>{{cite news| last = Siler| first = Ross| title = Utah Jazz: Brewer emerging to fill void at the two| publisher = The Salt Lake Tribune| date = October 26, 2007| url = http://www.sltrib.com/sports/ci_7290129| access-date = November 18, 2007| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120928095339/http://www.sltrib.com/sports/ci_7290129| archive-date = September 28, 2012}}</ref> he assumed the role of Utah's starting [[shooting guard]]. By mid-November 2007, he was averaging double figures in [[point (basketball)|points]] and was among the NBA leaders in [[steal (basketball)|steals]]. He was later selected to play in the [[2008 NBA All-Star Game#T-Mobile Rookie Challenge|2008 Rookie-Sophomore Game]]. On February 28, 2009, Brewer recorded a career-high 26 points, along with 7 rebounds and 4 steals against the Sacramento Kings.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090304183112/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290228026 Brewer posts career high as Jazz end somber day with win over Kings]</ref>

===Memphis (2010)===
On February 18, 2010, he was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for a protected future first-round pick. His playing time declined late in the season due to a [[hamstring]] injury and the Grizzlies' fading playoff hopes.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/021810_grizzlies_acquire_ro_2010_02_18.html |title=Grizzlies acquire Ronnie Brewer from Jazz |work=NBA.com |date=February 18, 2010 | access-date= February 19, 2010}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2010–2012)===
On July 19, 2010, Brewer signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=6260 Bulls sign Ronnie Brewer]</ref> In his first season with the Bulls, Brewer played back up shooting guard, averaged 22 minutes per game, and was among the league leaders in defensive efficiency.

On July 10, 2012, the Bulls declined Brewer's option for the next season, along with teammate [[C.J. Watson]]'s option.<ref>K.C. Johnson. "[https://web.archive.org/web/20120713111753/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2012-07-10/sports/ct-spt-0711-bulls-chicago--20120711_1_decline-options-brewer-and-watson-gar-forman It's official: Brewer and Watson gone]". ''Chicago Tribune''. July 10, 2012. Retrieved on July 22, 2012.</ref>

===New York Knicks (2012–2013)===
On July 25, 2012, Brewer signed with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>[http://knicksnow.com/posts/1627/knicks-sign-ronnie-brewer Knicks Sign Ronnie Brewer] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120727225736/http://knicksnow.com/posts/1627/knicks-sign-ronnie-brewer |date=July 27, 2012 }}</ref>

On September 7, 2012, it was announced that Brewer would be out for six weeks after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2012/09/08/sports/basketball/knicks-ronnie-brewer-out-for-six-weeks.html Knicks’ Brewer Out for Six Weeks]</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2013)===
On February 21, 2013, the Oklahoma City Thunder acquired Brewer from the New York Knicks in exchange for a 2014 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_acquisitions_130222.html | title=Thunder Acquires Ronnie Brewer and Trade Exception in Separate Deals with Knicks and Blazers | work=NBA.com | date=February 21, 2013| access-date=February 25, 2013}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2013–2014)===
On August 28, 2013, Brewer signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-add-brewer Rockets Add Brewer]</ref> On February 21, 2014, he was waived by the Rockets.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/usa/nba/74500/rockets-waive-ronnie-brewer-and-sign-troy-daniels.html Rockets waive Ronnie Brewer and sign Troy Daniels]</ref>

===Return to Chicago (2014)===
On April 7, 2014, Brewer signed with the Chicago Bulls for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-brewer-remainder-season.html BULLS SIGN BREWER FOR REMAINDER OF THE SEASON]</ref> On July 15, 2014, he was waived by the Bulls.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-amundson-brewer-and-james BULLS WAIVE AMUNDSON, BREWER AND JAMES]</ref>

===Santa Cruz Warriors (2015–2016)===
On October 31, 2015, Brewer was selected by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] in the second round of the [[2015 NBA Development League Draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-nba-d-league-draft-board/|title=2015 NBA D-League Draft Board|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2015|access-date=October 31, 2015|archive-date=October 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022072934/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-nba-d-league-draft-board/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==The Basketball Tournament==
Ronnie Brewer played for Team Arkansas in the 2018 edition of [[The Basketball Tournament]]. In 2 games, he averaged 8 points, 5 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game. Team Arkansas reached the second round before falling to the Talladega Knights.

==Coaching career==
On July 20, 2021, Brewer was hired by his alma mater, the University of Arkansas, as the recruiting coordinator for the men's basketball team under head coach [[Eric Musselman]]. Prior to the start of the 2023–24 season, Brewer was promoted to assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2023/sep/26/ua-hoops-staffers-earn-promotion-to-assistant/ |title=UA hoops staffers earn promotion to assistant | Arkansas Democrat Gazette |date=September 26, 2023 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brewer is cousins with Detroit rapper [[Guilty Simpson]].
